items.title: Enriques-Severi-Zariski: vanishing of H^1 of sufficiently negative twists of an ample invertible sheaf under depth at least two
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma, attributed by the author to Enriques-Severi-Zariski, proves that for a proper scheme X over a field, an ample invertible sheaf L and a coherent F whose stalks have depth at least two at all closed points, one has H^1(X, F tensor L^{tensor m}) = 0 for m sufficiently negative. The proof embeds X into projective space so that L becomes a power of the restriction of O(1), reduces to a coherent module G on projective space built from the e twists of F, checks that G again has depth at least two at closed points and infinite depth off the image, and then carries out the projective-space case (proof lines 11168-11290). H3: the reduction step that packages the e twists into a single sheaf with controlled depth, followed by the projective-space vanishing argument, is independent research-level work.
